original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Add one charged operation family, a fused two-root readout y_m += A_m(z1+z2) with free source-port choice, to the five-source dirty connector; determine whether the all-31-mask batch reaches 72 map calls and the exact fused-read price of doing so.
scope_change_reason: The card's question is answered for one named operation family, the fused two-root sum readout, at the five-source all-31-mask batch; the favorable-budget part is reduced to an explicit price threshold rather than a physical comparison.
bottleneck_link: Side result for recursive-interface cost: the fused readout lowers the five-source batch to the 72 map-call floor, but needs at least 30 fused reads, so it can change a recursive connector bill only where a native fused read costs under about a fifth of a root transfer. No selected supplier is changed.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exact layer: the fused-read minimum at 72 map calls. The 73-call layer, physical prices and caller integration are left as open questions.
evidence: Written proof of the 72-call floor and the 30-fused-read lower bound; exhaustive census of 945 ten-call words x 30 ordered root assignments (minimum 30, attained by 310 cases on 135 words); symbolic arbitrary-map replay and 600 dense dirty F2 replays of the literal schedule built on PR943's ten-call word; five mutation controls rejected. Command: python3.12 -B research/two-root-sum-readout-connector/verify.py.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the minimum number of fused reads at 73 map calls, where one output may be read once from each of z1, z2 and the sum?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It gives the next point of the (map calls, fused reads) frontier between the 72-call cost of 30 and the 74-call cost of 0.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the census with one triple-read output whose mask is q1_s + q2_t + q_u, then add four-read outputs for the 74-call layer.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; the triple-read placements add an 11^3 factor per word and root assignment.

open_questions.question: Does any caller supply a native fused read whose surcharge is below about one fifth of a root transfer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only then can 30 fused reads beat the credited eight- or six-transfer two-root endpoints.
open_questions.first_step: Name one caller whose A_m leaf can consume z1 + z2 in a single pass and price that pass against a transfer at the same ports.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical instance of this connector interface or measured port prices.

open_questions.question: Can a mixed schedule with a few transfers and a few fused reads beat both endpoints at intermediate price ratios?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two mechanisms are priced by different quantities; a mixture may dominate on part of the ratio range.
open_questions.first_step: Add transfer calls to this census's state model and minimize t*sigma + f*phi over a grid of ratios.
open_questions.blocked_by: The transfer state space is larger than the 945-word census; PR1615's skeleton enumeration is a starting point.
